Michael: Quick results from the precision sweep (fp16, bf16, int8, fp8) for Cedar13b and Nova40b across H100 (us-east-1) and A100 (eu-west-1). Posting the short summary + config we used.

Sam: Nice — TL;DR numbers?

Michael: TL;DR: fp8 gives the best perf/quality trade on H100, INT8 is very competitive on A100 with slightly better quality. Rough numbers (relative to fp16 baseline):
- Nova40b @ H100 (seq=2048, batch=1): fp8 ~2.1x tokens/sec, p99 +12ms vs fp16, QA EM delta -0.6 pts.
- Nova40b @ A100 (seq=2048, batch=1): int8 ~1.8x tokens/sec, p99 +20ms, QA EM delta -0.2 pts.
- Cedar13b: fp8 on H100 ~1.9x, INT8 on A100 ~1.6x; bf16 ~= fp16 quality.

Anya: How did you measure "QA EM"? dataset + eval script?

Michael: Eval set = 3k QA pairs sampled from staging prompts (mix of open-domain + instruction). We run deterministic sampling (top_p 0.0, temp 0.0) and compute EM. Script: `tools/evals/qa_em.py --preds preds.json --gold gold.json`. Seed pinned.

Natalie: Kernel choices? any difference in perf by kernel?

Michael: Yes. On H100 we used `kernels/auto_opt_v2` which unlocked fp8-friendly fused attention kernels. Switching from legacy to auto_opt_v2 reduced p99 by ~12ms and increased throughput ~8%. On A100 we stayed on `kernels/compat_v1` for INT8 due to stability; upgrading to `compat_v2` netted another ~4% throughput.

bench-bot: run_id=run-2026-03-15-08-31, config=[nova40b, seq2048, batch1, kv_cache=on, kernels=auto_opt_v2/compat_v1], artifacts: s3://bench/nova40b/2172345678/*.png, csv.

Lee: Did you enable prefix/KV caching in these runs? That can swing p50 a lot for short-turn workloads.

Michael: KV cache enabled. For fairness we used two modes: '
- cold-start (no kv cache) for end-to-end latency
- warmed-cache (kv cache primed) for steady-state throughput
Results quoted above are steady-state (warmed). Cold-start p99s are ~18-25% higher.

Sam: Capacity planning numbers? suppose a customer needs 1k sustained RPS with avg seq 512.

Michael: Back-of-envelope: (using tokens/sec from our steady-state throughput scaled to seq512)
- H100 fp8: ~12 GPUs for 1k RPS
- H100 fp16: ~22 GPUs for 1k RPS
- A100 int8: ~15 GPUs for 1k RPS
- A100 bf16: ~24 GPUs for 1k RPS
These assume 95th pct CPU+IO headroom preserved and batching tuned to 32-64.

Anya: Any quality regressions beyond EM? e.g., safety/hallucination?

Michael: Quick checks: ROUGE-L on summarization set ~ -0.3 pts for fp8, hallucination proxy (n-gram exact match to gold) shows tiny uptick for extreme int8 settings (int8-aggressive qprofile). We kept int8-safe profile for reported numbers. Will run full eval suite next.

Natalie: Are there configuration snippets (deploy) you can drop here?

Michael: Paste of the staging config we used:
```
model: nova40b
precision_profile: fp8-balanced  # options: fp16, bf16, int8-safe, int8-aggressive, fp8-balanced
kernel_policy: auto_opt_v2
kv_cache: true
batching: {max_tokens: 65536, prefer_small_batch: false}
autoscale: off
metrics: perf,p99,p95,em,rouge
```

Lee: Any instability observed? OOMs, silent corruption, divergence?

Michael: No OOMs with current qprofiles. int8-aggressive caused ~0.2% token-level NaN/inf anomalies on Nova during one exploratory run; we rolled that back. fp8-balanced stable on H100 for 48h soak.

Sam: Next steps?

Michael: Action items: 
- (Michael) push fp8-balanced Nova40b image to staging canary (today) :white_check_mark:
- (Anya) run full eval suite (5k QA + 2k summarization) for fp8 and int8-safe on both GPUs (by EOD Thu)
- (Natalie) sanity-check kernel upgrade path for A100 compat_v2 in staging (this week)
- (Lee) update capacity calc script with these new throughputs and rerun cost model (by Mon)

bench-bot: summary artifact: s3://bench/summary/2172345678-summary.csv

Sam: Perfect. If fp8 hits the quality bar on the larger eval we should consider a controlled canary rollout on Dedicated H100 pools.

Michael: Agreed. I'll capture the eval artifacts and open a PR with the perf dashboard links.

Anya: Thanks — will start the large eval now.

Natalie: I'll coordinate the kernel rollout plan.

Lee: I'll update the capacity spreadsheet after Anya's numbers.

Michael: thanks all :rocket:
